title: Grateful Dead Live at Purdue University on 1969-04-18
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent 1969 Purdue soundboard capture with a groovy set highlighted by Hard to Handle, King Bee, Lovelight and an uninterrupted Other One, though Jerry’s guitar sometimes recedes.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller SBD transfer delivers clear, punchy mix that lets Pigpen’s bluesy swagger and the band’s tight groove shine. Highlights include a scorching Hard to Handle with slick slide work, King Bee, Lovelight and a fast‑paced Other One that flows straight into an epic Morning Dew. A few listeners note occasional buried Jerry parts and possible splicing of the last three cuts, but overall the performance is energetic and memorable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the show’s energy, setlist highlights and excellent soundboard mix; only a few mention minor balance issues or possible track swaps, yielding an overall strong but not flawless rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is generally crisp and well‑balanced (Charlie Miller transfer); occasional moments where Jerry’s guitar is buried and the last three tracks may be from another source, but overall clarity is high.

standout_songs: That's It For The Other One / The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set moves with a steady groove, featuring bluesy Pigpen numbers early and building to an uninterrupted Other One that leads into a soaring Morning Dew; a mid‑show circuit‑breaker break adds a quirky anecdote but does not disrupt the overall momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Some reviewers note Jerry’s guitar can be hard to hear at times, though his slide work on Hard to Handle is praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass shines, especially during the opening of The Other One after the drum solo; one reviewer interviewed him backstage and described him as being in another world.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen (keys) delivers bluesy buzz‑saw riffs on Hard to Handle, King Bee and Lovelight, with his vocal enthusiasm highlighted throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: No specific drum commentary beyond the circuit‑breaker incident that cut sound mid‑song.
